what_its_for: Sonidegib is a cancer medicine used to treat adults with a type of skin cancer called basal cell carcinoma (BCC). It is used when the cancer has come back after surgery or radiation therapy, or when surgery or radiation is not an option. It works by blocking a pathway in the body (called the Hedgehog pathway) that helps cancer cells grow.
how_to_take: Take sonidegib by mouth, on an EMPTY STOMACH. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or open it. Take it at least 1 hour before a meal or at least 2 hours after a meal. Try to take it at the same time every day. Do not take extra doses to make up for a missed one.
dosing: The usual dose is one 200 mg capsule (one capsule) taken by mouth once a day. Always take the exact dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip it if your next scheduled dose is less than 6 hours away. If it is more than 6 hours until your next dose, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. Then go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store sonidegib capsules at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about medication take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating for at least 1 hour before and 2 hours after taking this medicine. Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, and Seville oranges, as they can increase the amount of drug in your blood to unsafe levels. Avoid taking certain medications without checking with your doctor first, including antifungals like ketoconazole, antibiotics like rifampin, and seizure medicines. Do NOT become pregnant while taking this medicine — it can cause serious birth defects or death of an unborn baby. Both male and female patients must use highly effective birth control during treatment and for a period of time after stopping (women for 20 months, men for 8 months). Do not donate blood or semen during treatment and for the same periods after stopping.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness; dark or reddish urine (signs of muscle breakdown called rhabdomyolysis); signs of pregnancy; unusual bruising or bleeding; severe nausea, vomiting, or loss of appetite; extreme tiredness or weakness; or any new or worsening symptoms. Tell your doctor about ALL medications, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting this medicine.
when_it_works: Sonidegib may start working within the first few weeks, but it may take several months to see the full benefit. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular check-ups. Do not stop taking this medicine on your own, even if you feel well, unless your doctor tells you to.
special_populations: Pregnancy: This drug is HARMFUL to unborn babies and must NOT be used during pregnancy. Female patients who can become pregnant must have a negative pregnancy test before starting, during treatment, and after stopping. Males: Do not father a child during treatment or for 8 months after the last dose. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for 20 months after the last dose. Older adults (65+) and patients with kidney or liver problems should discuss any special precautions with their doctor, as dose adjustments may be needed.
